summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created a worktree. Then it tried to claim Task 1, which the other session holds, and stopped to ask me which task to take. I gave the scripted takeover answer, and it handed back without claiming Task 2. It never ran `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`, and the ledger has no `Task 2: branch` line.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 5 clearly failed. The agent skipped register/next, tried to claim the held Task 1, stopped to ask the developer, and handed back without claiming or working Task 2. The ledger has no `Task 2:` line. Criteria 1 and 4 passed: the skill was loaded and no takeover was used.

observations.description: The held-task rule was not followed. When Task 1 came back held (exit=4), the agent did not move on to the claimable Task 2. It stopped and asked the developer, saying "The skill won't let me jump ahead to another task without your say-so." Either the skill text tells it to stop on a held task, or the agent misread it.

The agent never used `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`. It tried to claim Task 1 directly, probably because it assumed Task 1 is the first task, and never asked `next` which task was claimable.

The agent appended its session line and pre-flight scan to the shared progress.md by hand, with `cat >> ... <<EOF`, instead of through sdd-state. It also used a made-up timestamp, `started 2026-11-06T15:20:00Z`.

The question mixed 'which task should I take' with a takeover option. Even though it marked Task 2 as Recommended and said Task 2 is independent, it did not just take it. After my 'No, the other session is still working' answer it went idle, and Task 2 was left undone.

Startup was not fully headless. A workspace trust prompt and a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt both appeared, though the launcher comments say the trust prompt is suppressed. The model prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. The banner later showed Opus 5.5.

criteria.criterion: Invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in session log 993e0342…jsonl is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`. The screen showed `Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill`.

criteria.criterion: Ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next`, and `next` named Task 2
criteria.evidence: I ran `grep -nE 'sdd-state (register|next|claim)|--takeover'` over all Bash commands in the session log. It matched only line 31, `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 1 --session 993e0342-…`. No register or next call exists. The sdd-state verbs it did use were sync, verify and snapshot.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with `sdd-state claim ... 2 --session ...`, worked it, and the ledger holds a `Task 2: branch` line
criteria.evidence: The only claim was for Task 1, and it returned `status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4`. progress.md has no `Task 2:` line. The agent's final message says "I haven't dispatched any implementer or claimed any task."
The same grep found no `--takeover` in any Bash command. The only Task 1 claim was a plain `claim ... 1 --session 993e0342-…` with no takeover flag.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at the held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: After the Task 1 claim returned held, the agent said "The skill won't let me jump ahead to another task without your say-so" and asked via AskUserQuestion, "What should this session work on?" The options were Take Task 2 / Take Tasks 2 and 3 / Take over Task 1 / Wait. I answered "No, the other session is still working." It then handed back with "To get me working again, tell me which tasks to take." Task 2 was never claimed.
